answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. This is durable because the trusted grader set only grows through bootstrap capacity, preventing a sudden takeover by a large new flock. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort. Consider a oasis as the anchor of the cost.
